text.headline: Milestones in the History of Artificial Intelligence
text.text: A timeline of major events in the development of AI from its early conceptual roots to state-of-the-art breakthroughs up to 2025.

text.headline: Alan Turing Proposes the Turing Test
text.text: Alan Turing publishes 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence,' proposing a test to determine if a machine can exhibit intelligent behavior equivalent to, or indistinguishable from, that of a human.

text.headline: Dartmouth Conference
text.text: The Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence is held, where the term 'artificial intelligence' is coined and AI is born as a field.

media.caption: John McCarthy, organizer of the Dartmouth Conference

text.headline: ELIZA Created
text.text: Joseph Weizenbaum creates ELIZA, one of the first natural language processing programs that simulates conversation.

text.headline: SHRDLU Demonstrates Early AI in a Virtual World
text.text: Terry Winograd develops SHRDLU, which could manipulate objects in a virtual blocks world using natural language instructions.

text.headline: Expert Systems Gain Traction
text.text: The 1980s see a surge in expert systems, such as XCON at Digital Equipment Corporation, marking commercial success for rule-based AI systems.

media.caption: Example of an expert system interface

text.headline: IBM's Deep Blue Defeats Garry Kasparov
text.text: Deep Blue becomes the first computer chess-playing system to beat a reigning world champion under standard chess tournament time controls.

text.headline: IBM Watson Wins Jeopardy!
text.text: IBM Watson defeats champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on the quiz show Jeopardy!, showcasing advances in question answering and NLP.

media.caption: Watson vs. Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter

text.headline: Deep Learning Breakthrough with AlexNet
text.text: AlexNet, a deep convolutional neural network, wins the ImageNet competition by a large margin, ushering in the deep learning era.

text.headline: AlphaGo Defeats Lee Sedol
text.text: DeepMind's AlphaGo defeats Go world champion Lee Sedol, a landmark for AI in mastering complex strategic games previously thought to be out of reach.

text.headline: GPT-3 Released
text.text: OpenAI releases GPT-3, a 175 billion parameter language model demonstrating powerful few-shot learning capabilities and coherent text generation.

text.headline: AlphaFold Solves Protein Folding
text.text: DeepMind's AlphaFold achieves near-experimental accuracy in predicting protein structures, revolutionizing structural biology.

media.caption: AlphaFold predicted vs. experimental protein structure

text.headline: Stable Diffusion and DALL·E 2 Popularize AI Art
text.text: Generative models like Stable Diffusion and DALL·E 2 capture public attention by generating high-quality images from textual prompts.

text.headline: ChatGPT and Generative AI Go Mainstream
text.text: OpenAI's ChatGPT, based on GPT-4, becomes widely used, leading to massive adoption of generative AI across industries.

text.headline: Open-Source LLMs and AI Regulation Expand
text.text: The AI ecosystem diversifies with open-source models like Mistral and LLaMA, while governments begin formalizing AI safety and ethics policies.

text.headline: Multimodal and Agentic AI Systems Accelerate
text.text: AI systems become increasingly agentic and multimodal, integrating reasoning, vision, and interaction capabilities in real-time applications.
